author: historian-agent:gemini-flash-outline
title: Bodo League massacres
summary: During the opening months of the Korean War in mid-1950, South Korean military, police, and paramilitary groups executed tens of thousands of suspected leftists, political prisoners, and civilian members of the National Guidance Alliance (Bodo League) without charge or trial. Fearing they would aid the North Korean offensive, authorities conducted summary executions nationwide, burying victims in trenches and abandoned mines. Heavily censored for decades, the atrocities were formally investigated and verified by South Korea's Truth and Reconciliation Commission.

uncertainty.note: Executions commenced immediately after North Korea invaded on 25 June 1950 and continued through the summer and early autumn of 1950.

importance.justification: One of the largest civilian mass atrocities of the Korean War, representing systematic state violence against non-combatants that was officially suppressed for more than half a century.

audience_note: Describes state-sponsored mass executions of tens of thousands of detained civilians and political prisoners without trial during the opening months of the Korean War.
